engine_name: SGLang (sgl-project), stable line v0.5.x (e.g. v0.5.4.post1 / v0.5.9 as of early-mid 2026; main has moved toward CUDA 13.0). High-throughput LLM inference engine from LMSYS/Stanford with RadixAttention prefix caching, continuous batching, and an OpenAI-compatible server.
cuda_128_compatible: Yes, but it is the non-default, increasingly legacy path and requires care. SGLang's newest releases (and the NVIDIA container line, e.g. 25.11) have shifted the DEFAULT to CUDA 13.0; the official docs now describe the standard pip install as CUDA 12.9. CUDA 12.8 (cu128) is NOT the happy path. Pre-built cu128 wheels DO exist: (a) PyTorch cu128 wheels via https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128, and (b) matching sgl-kernel cu128 wheels published on GitHub (https://github.com/sgl-project/whl/releases) and via the cu128 extra-index (https://sgl-project.github.io/whl/cu128 / https://docs.sglang.ai/whl/cu128/). So pip install is possible WITHOUT a full source build, e.g. `pip install 'sglang[all]==0.5.x' torch==2.8.0+cu128 --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 --extra-index-url https://sgl-project.github.io/whl/cu128` plus a force-reinstalled `sgl_kernel-<ver>+cu128` wheel. HOWEVER there are documented dependency-resolution conflicts on recent versions (Issue #25069, #25890): newer sglang pulls cuda-python==13.x and flashinfer cu13 builds that conflict with a cu128 torch, requiring careful version pinning to an older sglang/sgl-kernel pair (e.g. sgl-kernel 0.3.x cu128). Driver 570.195 / CUDA 12.8 runtime is sufficient to RUN cu128 wheels (no source build strictly needed if you pin a compatible older sglang). If you must build from source for cu128, it is a moderate-to-heavy build: clone, `pip install -e python`, then build sgl-kernel with cmake/ninja and `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.6` for the A6000 (sm_86) — slow (tens of minutes) and brittle. sm_86 (A6000/GA102) is a fully supported Ampere target. [uncertain] exact lowest sglang version that installs cleanly on cu128 without manual pinning.
gemma4_support: Yes. Gemma 4 support was merged via PR #21952 (JustinTong0323), covering the E2B, E4B, 26B-A4B (MoE), and 31B (dense) variants, including multimodal (text/image/audio) and hybrid reasoning. google/gemma-4-31B-it is explicitly listed. Required format: HuggingFace safetensors (NOT GGUF/EXL2 — SGLang loads HF-format weights). Quantization paths that exist for Gemma 4: FP8 block-quantized checkpoints (e.g. RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block on HF, referenced in SGLang's own bug reports) and AWQ W4A16 checkpoints (Gemma W4A16/AWQ checkpoints are noted as available). bitsandbytes online 4-bit/8-bit IS supported as a loader, but its int4 kernels on sm_86 (Ampere) are historically patchy and SGLang recommends AWQ/FP8 over bnb for best Ampere performance. Architectural note: SGLang auto-selects the Triton attention backend for Gemma 4 (required for bidirectional image-token attention during prefill) and uses dedicated gemma4 reasoning + tool-call parsers. The official cookbook reference config for the 31B dense model targets 2x H200 (TP=2) or 1x MI300X (TP=1) — i.e. it is sized for big GPUs, not explicitly validated single-A6000 at 48GB.
per_request_reasoning_toggle: Yes — works per-request and is a first-class documented feature. Server is launched with `--reasoning-parser gemma4`. Per request, pass `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}}` (or `false`) on the OpenAI /v1/chat/completions call. Setting `enable_thinking: false` per request reliably disables CoT and returns normal content; `enable_thinking: true` returns the reasoning trace via the `reasoning_content` field. This is the SAME mechanism Google documents for HF Transformers (enable_thinking in apply_chat_template), so it is well-aligned with the model's chat template. CAVEAT / known footgun: if enable_thinking is not explicitly set to false and the model default is thinking-on, some responses can come back with only `reasoning_content` populated and an empty `content` field, which can break naive OpenAI clients — set enable_thinking explicitly per request to avoid this.
per_request_reasoning_budget: No reliable per-request token cap. SGLang's documented per-request control for Gemma 4 is the binary on/off `enable_thinking` flag via chat_template_kwargs; there is no first-class `thinking_budget_tokens` / `reasoning_budget` parameter exposed for Gemma 4 in the SGLang OpenAI API as of mid-2026. The practical way to cap reasoning length is the generic `max_tokens` (which bounds total output, not specifically the reasoning span) — that is a blunt instrument, not a true reasoning budget. So SGLang shares llama.cpp's limitation here: you can toggle thinking off per request (which SGLang does well), but you cannot precisely cap the number of reasoning tokens per request. [uncertain] whether a budget param has landed on the bleeding-edge main branch.
tool_calling_support: Dedicated parser, comparable to vLLM's approach. Launch with `--tool-call-parser gemma4` (and `--reasoning-parser gemma4`). The gemma4 tool-call parser handles the Gemma 4 tool delimiters (the <|tool_call|> / <tool_call|> channel tokens) and supports streaming partial tool calls. Function/tool calling is officially supported for all Gemma 4 variants including 31B. Quality should be solid for non-speculative serving. KNOWN FAILURE MODE to watch: tool-call argument streaming bugs surface specifically when MTP/speculative decoding is combined with multi-tool auto-tool-choice (documented on the closely-related vLLM gemma4 path, Issue #41967, where the first tool call's argument deltas are dropped in streaming). The SGLang non-spec path does not have that specific reported bug, but the broader Gemma 4 + spec-decode combination is buggy on SGLang too (see known_issues_gemma4). Recommend running tool calling WITHOUT speculative decoding for reliability.
openai_api_compatible: Yes. SGLang exposes an OpenAI-compatible server with /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions and SSE streaming; designed as a near drop-in for openai-python / httpx asyncio clients. Default port is 30000 (override with --host/--port to 8000). Deviations to be aware of: (1) reasoning output is returned in a non-standard `reasoning_content` field (separate from `content`) when thinking is on; (2) the empty-`content` edge case when enable_thinking is on and not explicitly toggled (see reasoning_toggle) can surprise strict clients. Otherwise the chat/completions shape, tool_calls, and streaming format are standard.
continuous_batching: Yes — a core strength. SGLang does continuous batching plus RadixAttention prefix caching, chunked prefill, and a zero-overhead CPU scheduler. For an agent with up to ~10 concurrent users and 4-8 parallel sub-agents that share large system prompts / tool schemas, RadixAttention's automatic prefix reuse is a real win (it reuses the shared prefix KV across the concurrent requests). This is well beyond what is needed at this scale and is the main reason to pick SGLang over llama.cpp for concurrency.
installation_steps:
Host-native on CUDA 12.8, no Docker (pin to a cu128-compatible sglang to avoid the cuda13 dependency conflict):

# 1. Python 3.10+ venv
python3.11 -m venv ~/.sglang && source ~/.sglang/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip

# 2. PyTorch cu128
pip install torch==2.8.0 torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

# 3. SGLang (pin a version known to resolve on cu128; newer ones pull cuda13 deps)
pip install 'sglang[all]==0.5.4.post1' \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 \
  --extra-index-url https://sgl-project.github.io/whl/cu128

# 4. If sgl-kernel did not install a cu128 build, force the matching cu128 kernel wheel:
pip install https://github.com/sgl-project/whl/releases/download/v0.3.5/sgl_kernel-0.3.5+cu128-cp310-abi3-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl --force-reinstall --no-deps

# 5. (Optional, if pip resolution fails) build sgl-kernel from source for sm_86:
sudo apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libibverbs-dev
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git && cd sglang/sgl-kernel
pip install build wheel 'cmake<4.0' ninja scikit-build-core
export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST='8.6' MAX_JOBS=$(nproc)
python -m build --wheel --no-isolation && pip install --no-deps dist/sgl_kernel*.whl

Expect to spend time resolving the cuda-python / flashinfer version conflicts noted in Issues #25069 and #25890.
serve_command:
FP8 block-quant 31B on a single A6000 (fits 48GB better than bf16; non-speculative for tool-call reliability):

python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-block \
  --quantization modelopt_fp8 \
  --tp 1 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --context-length 16384 \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
  --tool-call-parser gemma4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --attention-backend triton

Notes: gemma4 reasoning/tool parsers give per-request enable_thinking + tool calling. mem-fraction-static 0.75-0.85 to leave room for the co-resident embedder/reranker; Triton backend is auto-selected for Gemma 4 anyway. Do NOT add --speculative-* flags (crashes, see known_issues_gemma4). For AWQ instead of FP8, use an AWQ W4A16 31B checkpoint and drop --quantization (config auto-detected). [uncertain] exact VRAM fit of FP8 31B + 16k KV on a single 48GB card with co-resident models.
speculative_decoding: Supported in general (NEXTN / EAGLE), and Gemma 4 ships paired `*-assistant` draft models (e.g. google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant) for NEXTN multi-token prediction. BUT it is currently BROKEN for Gemma 4 31B on SGLang: SGLang auto-promotes NEXTN to FROZEN_KV_MTP when it detects the Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM draft, then crashes on the first request with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` in frozen_kv_mtp_utils.py (draft_input.bonus_tokens is None) and SIGQUITs the server (Issue #24912, open). The overlap scheduler is also disabled with Frozen-KV MTP (spec v2 unsupported). The question's mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf is a GGUF/llama.cpp artifact and is NOT usable by SGLang (SGLang uses the HF-format assistant model, not GGUF). Bottom line: leave speculative decoding OFF on SGLang for Gemma 4 31B until #24912 is fixed. [uncertain] whether a fix has merged on main since the report.
known_issues_gemma4: (1) Speculative decoding crash: NEXTN auto-promoted to FROZEN_KV_MTP -> first-request crash (`bonus_tokens is None`) in frozen_kv_mtp_utils.py, server killed (sgl-project/sglang #24912, open). (2) Empty `content` field: with thinking on and enable_thinking not explicitly toggled, /v1/chat/completions can return only reasoning_content and empty content, breaking strict OpenAI clients (general Gemma 4 hybrid-reasoning behavior; mirrors mlx-lm #1352). (3) Tool-call argument streaming under spec-decode: the gemma4 + MTP + multi-tool auto-tool-choice combo drops the first tool call's argument deltas in streaming (documented on vLLM #41967; risk applies to the shared Gemma 4 spec-decode design). (4) CUDA versioning churn: cu128 dependency conflicts (cuda-python 13.x / flashinfer cu13) on recent sglang releases (#25069, #25890) make cu128 install fiddly. (5) Slow model load: SGLang loads weights much slower than llama.cpp (minutes vs seconds) — startup friction, not runtime.
vram_usage: Rough estimates on the 48GB A6000 at 16k context, single stream: BF16 31B weights alone are ~62GB and will NOT fit on one A6000 (hence the cookbook's 2x H200 reference). FP8 block-quant 31B weights ~31-33GB, leaving roughly ~12-15GB for KV cache at 16k + overhead — feasible single-card but tight. AWQ/INT4 W4A16 31B weights ~16-18GB, leaving ~25GB+ for KV and headroom — the most comfortable single-A6000 option. Co-resident BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (~0.13GB) + bge-reranker-v2-m3 (~2.3GB) ~2.4GB total: fits alongside an INT4/AWQ deployment comfortably; with FP8 it is tight and you should drop --mem-fraction-static to ~0.70-0.75. [uncertain] precise numbers depend on quant checkpoint and batch concurrency.
small_scale_fit: Marginal-to-viable but heavier than warranted. SGLang's design center is high-concurrency cluster/datacenter serving (it is explicitly 'not created for enthusiasts running models on home rigs'). For 1 dev + up to 10 concurrent users it works and the concurrency/throughput headroom is generous, but the operational overhead is real: cu128 dependency pinning/source builds, slow model loads, FP8/AWQ checkpoint sourcing (no GGUF), and the spec-decode bug. Single-A6000 also forces a quantized checkpoint (bf16 31B won't fit). Migrating later to a personal A6000 is fine (same sm_86 target). Compared to a llama.cpp baseline, SGLang gives materially better concurrent throughput and RadixAttention prefix reuse, at a clear cost in setup/maintenance complexity.
overall_recommendation: VIABLE (not RECOMMENDED for this specific small/host-native CUDA-12.8 deployment). Pros: best-in-class continuous batching + RadixAttention prefix caching (big win for 4-8 sub-agents sharing prompts/tool schemas), genuine OpenAI-compatible API, dedicated gemma4 reasoning + tool-call parsers, reliable per-request enable_thinking on/off, broad quant support (FP8/AWQ). Cons that hold it below RECOMMENDED here: (1) CUDA 12.8 is now the legacy/off-default path with documented dependency conflicts — install is fiddly and may need version pinning or a source build; (2) NO per-request reasoning-token BUDGET (only on/off) — does not solve the core llama.cpp limitation, just the toggle half; (3) speculative decoding for Gemma 4 31B is currently broken (#24912), so the MTP speedup is off the table; (4) HF-format only (no GGUF), and bf16 31B doesn't fit a single 48GB A6000 so you must run FP8/AWQ; (5) operationally heavier than the llama.cpp baseline for a 1-dev / <=10-user scale. Net: choose SGLang if concurrent throughput and prefix-cache reuse across parallel sub-agents are the priority and you accept the setup overhead; otherwise vLLM (also gemma4 parsers, smoother on 12.x) or the llama.cpp baseline are simpler. If chosen, run on a pinned cu128 sglang, FP8 or AWQ 31B, parsers on, speculative decoding OFF.
